lines.text: Ask an AI for a source, and it might give you one that doesn't exist. Title, author, even page numbers.

phrases.text: Ask an AI for a source,
and it might give you one that doesn't exist.
Title, author, even page numbers.

lines.text: It isn't lying. It's doing what it was built to do.

phrases.text: It isn't lying.

lines.text: Here's why AI sometimes makes things up.

phrases.text: Here's why AI sometimes makes things up.

lines.text: A language model writes by predicting the next token, using patterns learned from huge amounts of text.

phrases.text: A language model writes by predicting the next token,
using patterns learned from huge amounts of text.

lines.text: Facts that appeared again and again leave strong patterns, so those answers are usually right.

phrases.text: Facts that appeared again and again leave strong patterns,
so those answers are usually right.

lines.text: But rare facts, like a small study or an obscure date, leave weak patterns. The model still has to write something, so it writes what a right answer would sound like.

phrases.text: But rare facts, like a small study or an obscure date, leave weak patterns.

so it writes what a right answer would sound like.
Researchers call this a hallucination.

lines.text: And many tests used to train and rank AI reward a confident guess over "I'm not sure."

lines.text: Tools that search the web or your documents first can help. But no AI is right every time.

lines.text: So use AI for ideas and drafts. For facts that matter, check the source, and make sure it's real.
